source_locator: Summary pages, Mayor of Sacramento (page 11), WITH 347 OF 347 PRECINCTS COUNTED, countywide total column; Certification of Elections Official dated June 21, 2012
verification_note: Votes from the county canvass dated June 21, 2012. Winner holds a majority of votes cast for all mayoral candidates in the primary (nominating) election, so the primary elected the mayor. Rule: the City Clerk's Ranked Choice Voting for Sacramento Act document (proposed charter amendment text, section 152(a)(13)) restates the nominating-primary procedure: a mayoral candidate who receives a majority of the votes cast for all candidates at the primary is declared elected by the council; otherwise the top two go to the November Regular Municipal Election. The same document finds that 44 percent of sitting city elected offices were filled by a candidate elected during the primary. The text is shown as proposed new text in italics, so it is a restatement of the procedure and not the charter page itself; the archived Charter text itself could not be opened (amlegal HTTP 403, municode returns no text). The county's qualified candidate list for the Nov 6, 2012 general election lists only City Council Districts 2 and 4 and a Charter Commission for the City of Sacramento; it lists no mayoral contest. No runoff or general mayoral round was held in 2012. Vote figures are from the county statement.
total_votes_basis: sum of Johnson 40,823, Rewers 16,551, Padilla 8,989, Jones 2,679 and write-in 459, countywide total column (all Sacramento city mayoral votes); Johnson share recomputes to 58.74 percent as printed
